subtitulo: The densest frame in the module: one word turns any dish on the menu into the dish you actually want
cena: The dish you want is on the menu with one ingredient in it that you do not eat, and the waiter is already writing.
frasePiso: You do not have to describe the meal you want. Point at the one on the menu and subtract.

clique.desconto: Nobody taught you a sentence for every dish you might want changed. You learned to subtract, and the menu became editable.
clique.piso: Next time something on a menu is nearly right, you will not order it as printed and pick around it. You will remove the part you do not want, in one word.

steps.pt: Most of what you want to say at a table is not a new dish. It is a dish on the menu, minus one thing.
The frame is senza, plus the thing you do not want. Without — and then the ingredient.

steps.promptPt: The salad is right except for one ingredient. Subtract it. Speak now.

steps.pt: Of course, no onion. Anything else?
The frame does not care what follows. Any ingredient, any drink, any dish — the word in front never changes.

steps.promptPt: Same frame, a drink this time: no ice. Speak now.
Ask whether there is a gluten-free version. Speak now.

steps.pt: Senza glutine is on packaging and menus everywhere. It is the one subtraction Italy already had a printed label for.
The opposite direction works too. Con adds, and più asks for more of something already there.

steps.promptPt: Add something instead of removing it: with lemon. Speak now.
Ask for a little more bread. Speak now.
steps.es: Un po' più di pane, per favore.
steps.pinyin: oon po pyoo dee PA-ne per fa-VO-re
steps.tts: Un po' più di pane, per favore.

steps.promptPt: The pasta comes with cheese on top and you would rather it did not. Speak now.

steps.es: Il formaggio è già dentro. Le faccio un altro primo?
steps.pt: The cheese is already in it. Shall I do you a different first course?
steps.tts: Il formaggio è già dentro. Le faccio un altro primo?
steps.acao: Take the alternative dish they are offering.

steps.pt: Sometimes the answer is no, and the reason is that it was cooked in. Take the alternative they offer — that is the sentence doing its job.

steps.promptPt: Ask whether they can do it without butter. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can it be done without butter?

steps.promptPt: You want the flat kind of bottled water, not the fizzy kind. Order it. Speak now.

steps.es: Senza cipolla, per favore. Senza ghiaccio, per favore. Acqua senza gas, per favore.
steps.pinyin: SEN-tsa chee-POL-la. SEN-tsa gee-AT-cho. AK-kwa SEN-tsa gas per fa-VO-re
steps.pt: Shadow one word carrying three completely different requests.
steps.tts: Senza cipolla, per favore. Senza ghiaccio, per favore. Acqua senza gas, per favore.

steps.pt: B12 done. Senza subtracts, con adds, più asks for more — and the menu stops being a fixed list.

secoes.corpo: Ingredient, drink, whole category — the word in front is always the same and never changes shape. This is why it carries more of the module than any other frame.

secoes.titulo: Con and più are the other two directions
secoes.corpo: Con adds, più asks for more of what is already there. Together with senza you can adjust nearly anything on a table without producing a full sentence.
Naturale or senza gas is still; frizzante or con gas is sparkling. Asking for water without saying which usually gets you a question back rather than a default.

secoes.titulo: Cooked in is a real no
secoes.corpo: If an ingredient is part of the sauce rather than on top, senza is not possible and the kitchen will say so — usually while offering something else. That offer is the useful part of the exchange.

permissao: You are allowed to change a dish. Asking for something senza an ingredient is a normal restaurant request in Italy, not a challenge to the kitchen — and it is far more comfortable for everyone than ordering as printed and leaving half of it.
espelho: Anyone who has ordered something at home and quietly picked out the ingredient they do not eat knows why this frame matters. The reluctance to modify is not about Italian — it is about not wanting to be a nuisance, in any language.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You ask for a dish without an ingredient and the waiter pauses, then suggests a different dish entirely.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I have asked for something unreasonable and they are steering me away.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: In Italian kitchens many ingredients are cooked into the base rather than added at the end. When the answer is è già dentro, the substitution being offered is the practical version of your request, not a refusal of it.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Take the alternative, or ask si può fare senza…? about the specific thing so the kitchen can answer for that dish rather than in general.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You end up with something that was actually made without the ingredient, instead of a dish that technically had it removed from the top.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not for an allergy, where a polite substitution is not enough and the request has to be unambiguous — that is what the next part is for.
